name: MMStar
description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 challenging samples meticulously selected by humans. It benchmarks 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs’ multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples.
creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
citeAs: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao. Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv:2403.20330v2, 2024.
rai:dataCollection: Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline. The authors first choose two benchmarks focused on natural images and four centered on scientific and technical knowledge for sample collection. They employ two closed-source LLMs and six open-source LLMs sizing 20B or larger as inspectors for visual dependency and LLM leakage. Samples with hit counts of two or fewer are retained after coarse filtering, reducing the pool from 22,401 to 11,607. Then three experts manually review samples to ensure visual dependency, comprehensive capability coverage, and advanced multimodal difficulty, and manually curate 1,500 high-quality samples.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The benchmark is constructed from samples selected from six existing benchmarks: MMBench, SEED, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, and MathVista.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The collected samples are filtered with an automated pipeline using LLM inspectors for visual dependency and leakage. Samples that could be answered by more than 2 of the 8 LLMs are excluded. The remaining coarsely filtered samples are evaluated by 16 LVLMs and split into four difficulty categories: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). Final selection considers both diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors develop an automated pipeline to preliminarily filter out samples that do not meet visual dependency and minimal leakage criteria. Open-source LLM inspectors are applied with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy to minimize response refusals and ensure consistency in answer formatting. Only samples with hit counts of two or fewer are retained. All questions are ensured to be converted into a multiple-choice format.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conduct manual review to ensure each sample’s answer should be based on understanding visual content, selected samples cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions, and most samples require advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution. The final benchmark is organized into 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To expedite manual selection of samples with varying difficulty levels, the authors tally the hit counts of all 16 LVLMs on the coarsely filtered samples and split them into four difficulty categories: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). Final selection considers diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: In the future, the authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM and LVLM training corpora.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper argues that inappropriate questions and data leakage can lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal performance gains and potentially misguide the study of LVLMs. It states that for research to be transparent and equitable, it is imperative to account for and mitigate such leakage.
rai:dataBiases: The paper identifies two major issues in existing benchmarks: many samples do not require visual content and some samples are unintentionally leaked into LLM and LVLM training data. It also notes that MMBench registers the highest average multi-modal gain, indicating significant overlap between domains covered by existing LVLM training data and MMBench.
rai:dataLimitations: Even on MMStar, no LVLMs managed to reach a passing average score in fine-grained perception, logical reasoning, science and technology, and mathematics, highlighting these dimensions as particularly challenging. The paper also notes that existing benchmarks can contain vision-independent samples and leaked samples, which can cause unfair comparisons and misjudgments.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended as a benchmark for evaluating large vision-language models’ multimodal capabilities. It is used for evaluation of 16 leading LVLMs on accuracy and on the proposed multi-modal gain and multi-modal leakage metrics, and is intended to provide a comprehensive and fair arena for comparing existing LVLMs.
